text:
Senator Mike Rounds highlights visits with veterans, disability advocates, and students in recent posts
Senator Mike Rounds, who represents South Dakota in the U.S. Senate and previously served two terms as governor of the state, recently shared updates on his activities across South Dakota through a series of posts on social media.
On June 22, 2026, Senator Rounds attended a major veterans' event in Mitchell. He wrote, "Enjoyed visiting Mitchell for the Department of South Dakota Veterans of Foreign Wars 96th Annual State Convention. It was great to join VFW members, Auxiliary members and veteran advocates from across the state and thank our veterans for their service and sacrifice on behalf of https://t.co/8fXQbPh9sV".
The following day, June 23, he met with disability services leaders in Pierre. In his post, he stated, "Visited with Liz Olive, CEO of Vista Care South Dakota based in Pierre. Important to hear directly about the challenges facing South Dakotans who rely on disability services. https://t.co/znYpX2roU7".
Later that same day, Senator Rounds highlighted student achievement at a national competition: "Enjoyed visiting with students from across South Dakota who are in town competing at the National History Day contest. Proud to see them representing South Dakota at the national level! https://t.co/bUwxVkNC5j".
Rounds is a lifelong resident of Huron, South Dakota, and is the eldest of 11 children. He holds a bachelor's degree in political science from South Dakota State University and has four children and eleven grandchildren (official website). In addition to his current Senate role, he serves on several key committees including Appropriations; Armed Services; Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs; Indian Affairs; and Intelligence.
